newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain forms National Guard to increase security.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain forms National Guard to increase security.

text.p: Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa on Tuesday ordered the formation of a National Guard to increase security in the Gulf Arab state.
A decree carried by the state-run Gulf News Agency said Sheikh Isa would be supreme commander of the force, an independent regular army.

"The National Guard force is considered part of the Bahrain Defence Force and...a shield to the security forces to protect the nation and maintain its safety, security and independence," the decree said.
Sheikh Isa also appointed one of his sons, Sheikh Mohammed, to head the force. The decree gave no further details.
Over the last two years Bahrain has faced civil unrest by members of its majority Shi'ite Moslem community seeking political and economic reforms from the Sunni-led government.
Nearly 30 people have been killed in sporadic violence including bombings and arson attacks. Hundreds of people have been detained.
Last week an arson attack in the Shi'ite village of Tubli killed an Asian worker and wounded two others.
